item.title: South Korea prepares market stabilisation funds after KOSPI hits 10-month low
item.description: In response to falling stock indices, South Korea's finance ministry is poised to activate market stabilisation funds. The KOSPI index has plummeted, marking its lowest point in the last ten months. An emergency meeting was convened by the finance minister to explore strategies for restoring investor confidence. Among the discussed actions are temporary regulations on stock buyback limits for publicly listed companies.

item.title: Crude oil futures brace for OPEC+ output decision amid supply glut concerns: Analysts
item.description: Next week promises to be a rollercoaster for crude oil futures as the OPEC+ meeting approaches. Traders are keeping a close eye on supply insights from the American Petroleum Institute and Energy Information Administration. Trading will be quiet on Tuesday due to Guru Nanak Jayanti. While concerns about a global supply surplus loom large, they overshadow geopolitical tensions in West Asia.

item.title: Why gold’s five-year winning streak is under threat after dramatic selloff
item.description: Gold has fallen to around $3,510 an ounce after hitting a record $5,594.82 earlier in 2026, putting it on track for its first annual loss in five years. A stronger dollar, elevated bond yields, profit-booking and weaker safe-haven demand continue to pressure prices.

item.title: InvIT IPO rush gathers pace; 4-5 private trusts likely to go public by Mar 2027
item.description: Four to five Infrastructure Investment Trusts are expected to launch public offerings to raise Rs 17,000 crore by 2027. These offerings aim to mobilise long-term capital for infrastructure development while appealing to a broader pool of investors. Notable companies like Brookfield and Investcorp are preparing to shift to public InvITs. In the past, InvITs raised around Rs 88,000 crore, demonstrating investor appetite.

item.title: 5 penny stocks plunge up to 68% in six months. Do you own any?
item.description: Five BSE Smallcap penny stocks have fallen between 21% and 68% in recent months. Kalind and Empower India led the declines, plunging 68% and 62%, respectively.

item.title: Reliance Brands FY26 revenue up 3.8% to Rs 3,390.9 crore; loss narrows to Rs 137 crore
item.description: Reliance Brands has marked a significant financial milestone, achieving a revenue of Rs 3,390.89 crore for FY26 and reducing losses. Operating more than 1,085 Points of Sale nationwide, the brand continues to collaborate with over 90 partner names. Recent acquisitions, including Hamleys and new entries like Stella McCartney and Fabletics, demonstrate the company’s drive to lead in the competitive fashion and lifestyle industry.

item.title: Anthropic's post-debut stumble delivers reality check for AI trade
item.description: Anthropic’s shares fell about 9% after their market debut, deepening concerns over stretched AI valuations and showing that even a marquee listing has not revived investor enthusiasm for the sector. The focus is now shifting to whether Anthropic can justify its roughly 40-times-sales valuation and whether a potential OpenAI IPO next year can restore appetite for AI stocks.

item.title: Nifty eyes 26,200 as rally strengthens; 6 sectors signal outperformance
item.description: Nifty surged 2.61% last week, gaining 656 points amid strong FII inflows and improving technical indicators. Resistance lies at 25,950–26,200, while banking, IT and financial services lead sectoral momentum. Analysts advise caution against chasing extended market gains.

item.title: Stocks to buy: HSBC lists 19 Indian stocks that saw FY27 earnings upgrades, check target prices
item.description: HSBC identified 19 Indian stocks with Buy ratings that received FY27 earnings upgrades after Q2 results. Ather Energy, GAIL and IIFL Finance led revisions, while improving corporate profitability highlighted a broadening earnings recovery across market capitalisations and sectors.

item.title: Concurrent Gainers: These 13 stocks gained for 5 days in a row, all rose over 27%
item.description: The Sensex gained 1.08% during the five sessions ending November 20, while 99 BSE 200 stocks advanced consecutively. Thirteen shortlisted stocks delivered impressive cumulative returns ranging from 27.51% to 31.02%, led by Sera Investments & Finance India.

item.title: AI to lead investment strategy in 2027; Energy and borrowing costs shape macro outlook: Barclays
item.description: According to the latest report from Barclays Private Bank, the impending year 2027 calls for a stronger investment focus on artificial intelligence. While infrastructure is steadily developing, the rising costs of debt financing could negatively impact the economics of these projects. The report warns of potential computing demand outpacing supply, which may hinder technology scalability. Investors should approach government bonds with caution due to elevated yields and inflation worries.

item.title: Market winners: Max Healthcare, Deepak Fertilisers among 10 stocks that surged up to 14% in last week
item.description: Max Healthcare, Deepak Fertilisers and Blue Star led Nifty 500 weekly gainers, surging 14.14%, 13.90% and 12.84%, respectively. Ten stocks outperformed the broader index, which gained 1.5%, highlighting strong momentum across healthcare, banking, real estate and other sectors.

item.title: US Treasury yields drop for day and week; AI trade concern spurs safe-haven bid
item.description: US Treasury yields experienced a significant decline due to heightened investor concerns surrounding the AI trade. As a result, investors shifted their focus towards safe-haven assets such as Treasury securities. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note fell below 5% for the first time in several months. Concerns about rising company debt and spending related to AI contributed to investor unease in recent weeks.

item.title: Dollar weaker as Fed-fueled rally stalls; lower US yields help yen
item.description: The US dollar has encountered a modest downturn, sliding to 103.86 as investor confidence wavers in the currency market. Despite this pullback, traders expect the Federal Reserve to maintain a hawkish stance in upcoming statements. Concurrently, Bitcoin has dipped below the $60,000 mark, sparking concerns about its valuation amidst ongoing market volatility.

item.title: Crude prices may normalise to USD 70 by end-2027 as global oil market moves into surplus: Report
item.description: Global crude oil prices are projected to normalize around USD 70 per barrel by the end of 2027. Rising non-OPEC+ supplies and declining Chinese oil demand are expected to lead to a market surplus. Refining margins are likely to remain elevated in the near term before gradual normalization occurs. Geopolitical tensions, particularly between the US and Iran, are likely to influence oil supply dynamics.

item.title: Gold's slide deepens as AI rout, rate-hike bets hurt bullion
item.description: Gold prices plummeted by 3% on Friday, settling at a 14-month low of $3,502.49 per ounce. This sharp decline is largely due to a hawkish interest rate forecast and a significant selloff within AI stocks. Analysts point to forced liquidations of gold holdings as a factor, alongside increasing expectations of US borrowing costs, contributing to the commodity's bearish trend this week.

item.title: UK stocks sink as global selloff weighs on banks and miners
item.description: UK stocks experienced significant declines on Friday, resulting from a global market selloff linked to AI valuations. The FTSE 100 index closed at a five-month low, influenced by sharp declines in banking and mining stocks. Despite stronger-than-expected UK retail sales, declines in sectors outweighed positive news. Defensive consumer companies offered some support amid broader financial concerns.

item.title: European shares post worst week in over a year as AI trade unravels
item.description: European shares declined sharply, reflecting deeper worries about the sustainability of AI-related investments and overall economic growth. Concerns intensified after Anthropic's initial public offering did not restore confidence in the tech sector. The overall market decline affected various sectors, including cyclical stocks and semiconductor companies, due to profit-taking by investors. Despite recent losses, the STOXX 600 index remains up year-to-date, surpassing the performance of the S&P 500.

item.title: Tech leads global stocks rout, Treasury yields fall
item.description: On Friday, global stock markets faced a harsh sell-off, notably impacting technology stocks. In response, US traders turned to safer investments as the 10-year yield sharply decreased. The Dow Jones Industrial Average took a major hit, alongside declines in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq. However, consumer staples emerged relatively unscathed within the S&P 500.

item.title: Wall Street Week Ahead: 'Black Friday' brings consumer spending into focus for AI-rocked market
item.description: As the holiday season draws near, investors are keenly watching consumer spending patterns amid rising inflation fears. With US retail sales expected to show a modest uptick, this hints at consumer strength. Major retailers express optimism about this year's holiday shopping, although high gasoline and energy costs may pose challenges for spending. Investors are analyzing economic signals to understand potential market effects in the upcoming week.

item.title: Sebi proposes limiting tenure of chief executives, independent directors of stock exchanges, market infrastruction institutions
item.description: India's Securities and Exchange Board is proposing crucial adjustments to governance norms affecting market institutions. Key suggestions include lowering the age threshold for public interest directors from 75 to 70 years, instituting a maximum of two three-year terms for directors, and restricting managing directors to an eight-year tenure. Current executives can finish their ongoing terms despite these proposed changes. SEBI is seeking public feedback on these recommendations by December 11.

item.title: Nasdaq tumbles 2% as Anthropic retreat deepens AI trade concerns
item.description: Following a rocky market debut, Anthropic’s stock price plunge led to a notable drop in the Nasdaq Composite index. The AI sector faces growing skepticism amidst high valuations and investment risks, putting pressure on major U.S. stock indexes. Despite some companies reporting strong earnings, investor anxiety persists over potential interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.

item.title: Nasdaq crashes 5% at close, erasing 2026 gains; S&P 500, Dow in correction: Stock Market Highlights
Rupee climbs past 93/USD as investors seek shelter in Indian stocks, shorts unwind
item.description: The Indian rupee has strengthened past the 93-per-dollar mark for the first time since April. This recovery is attributed to over $12 billion of foreign investments in Indian equities in November. Hedge funds have unwound bearish positions on the rupee, contributing to its recent gains. The Reserve Bank of India has taken measures to support the local currency amidst stabilization efforts.

item.title: Anthropic's debut rally fades as shares crack 7% in US pre-market trade
item.description: Anthropic shares fell as much as 7.4% in premarket trading on their second day, as a global market selloff and concerns over the AI trade overshadowed the optimism surrounding its record-setting IPO debut. After surging 39% from the IPO price on Thursday, the stock ended 17% higher. A steep valuation and competitive threats added to investor caution.

item.title: Sharp rupee appreciation may cut IT firms' FY27 earnings by up to 13%: Report
item.description: According to a new report, the appreciation of the Indian rupee could lead Indian IT companies to experience reduced earnings. The stronger rupee against foreign currencies may significantly impact profitability, especially for firms with substantial European exposure. As traditional cost-saving strategies grow scarce, maintaining margins will be a challenge, compounded by the current economic environment affecting pricing strategies in the industry.

item.title: Sebi plans consultation paper to remove FPI constraints absent in other markets
item.description: SEBI is set to release a consultation paper aimed at simplifying regulations for foreign portfolio investors. The goal is to eliminate certain compliance restrictions to enhance India's appeal to global investors. SEBI also plans to expedite the onboarding process, targeting completion in just five business days. Additionally, KYC review cycles for applicable FPIs will be extended, reducing repetitive compliance activities.

item.title: Indian finance hub eyes dual share model to kickstart public offers: Report
item.description: Indian regulators are currently assessing a new proposal that would allow companies to introduce dual-class shares for listings in both domestic markets and GIFT City. This initiative seeks to invigorate equity market activity in GIFT City, which has faced challenges regarding limited primary market participation. One class of shares would be traded in rupees, while the other would be dollar-denominated, granting foreign investors easier access alongside reduced tax implications.

item.title: Who is Roaring Kitty? The man behind GameStop's meme rally
item.description: Keith Gill, better known as Roaring Kitty, is back on social media after nearly two years. His cryptic Cat Mario post sent GameStop shares higher, reviving memories of the 2021 meme-stock rally and sparking fresh interest among retail investors.

Treasury rally spills over to Indian bonds, debt supply slows move
item.description: Indian government bonds saw slight gains, reflecting the upward trend in US Treasuries. Investors are keeping a close eye on the forthcoming weekly debt auction, pivotal for market movements. With retail inflation and fluctuating oil prices in play, the Reserve Bank of India may entertain further rate hikes. Although benchmark Brent crude holds steady, it remains vulnerable to geopolitical shifts, prompting caution among traders as they await auction results.

item.title: Rupee rises past 93 vs USD as portfolio inflows, bear retreat fuel rally
item.description: The Indian rupee has shown remarkable strength, breaking the 93 per dollar barrier for the first time since April. This positive shift was fueled by impressive foreign portfolio investments, exceeding $12 billion in November alone. Consequently, the rupee has left its Asian peers behind as it thrives against a strong dollar, all while navigating the Federal Reserve's anticipated hawkish stance, showcasing an encouraging signal for the Indian market.

item.title: Rupee strengthens 17 paise to 93.15 against US dollar in early trade
item.description: Rupee gained 17 paise to trade at 93.15 against the US dollar in early trade on Friday. The appreciation was supported by strong foreign fund inflows into the domestic equity markets. Despite higher crude prices and negative stock market sentiment, the currency showed resilience. Analysts expect slight positive bias in rupee trading due to declining crude and gold prices.

item.title: Anthropic shares close 17% higher on first day of trading amid protest, arrests outside Nasdaq
SELLAS Life Sciences shares plunge 19%: What triggered the sharp sell-off?
item.description: SELLAS Life Sciences shares plunged nearly 20% after the biotechnology company priced a $150 million public offering at $13 per share, a discount of around 28% to its previous close. The sell-off followed a sharp rally triggered by positive Phase 3 REGAL trial results for its experimental leukemia vaccine.
